newsitem.title: USA: Walgreen sees opening 230 stores in FY97.
newsitem.headline: Walgreen sees opening 230 stores in FY97.

text.p: Walgreen Co said Monday it expects to open a record 230 new Walgreens drug stores in fiscal 1997.

"We're projecting a record 230 new Walgreens to open this year," L. Daniel Jorndt, president, said in a statement. "Most of these will come in the second half of the year, which is the optimum building season across the country."

Jordnt said Walgreen opened 58 new stores during the fiscal first quarter ended November 30. Sixteen of the stores were relocations to more convenient, freestanding locations that typically generate higher sales and profitability, he added.
"By the year 2001 -- our 100th anniversary -- our average Walgreens will be only 5.7 years old -- compared to our average store age of 14.2 years in 1986," Jorndt said.
As of December 31, Walgreen operated 2,238 drug stores in 34 states and Puerto Rico, up from 2,117 a year ago.
Earlier, Walgreen reported earnings for the first quarter of $0.30 a share, up from $0.26 a year ago.

The company said strong net earnings were aided by good control of expenses and strong pharmacy sales, which advanced 17.5 percent for the quarter and 11.5 percent in comparable stores. Total comparable store sales advanced eight percent for the quarter.
